title: Go Digit General Insurance Ltd - 544179 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Digit reports FY26 IndAS-basis post-tax ROE of 17.7% and combined ratio 105.7%, but gross loss ratios are stable and motor OD loss ratio is rising amid retention cut to 89.6% from 95.9%.

summary.headline: Go Digit reports 17.7% post-tax ROE on Indian Accounting Standards basis for FY26 and a 105.7% combined ratio, with GDPI up 16.2%.
summary.overview: Management presented FY26 results re-based to Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS, effective 1 April 2026), which were audited for the first time, while stressing its internal KPIs remain NEP-based combined ratio plus DAC and IGAAP solvency. Full-year profit before tax on Ind AS plus DAC was INR239 crores in Q4 (vs INR142 crores) and post-tax profit was INR179 crores (vs INR106 crores). Q4 GDPI grew 21.3% and full-year GDPI grew 16.2%, while Q4 GWP growth slowed to about 6.2% because of a health reinsurance non-renewal. Solvency improved to 2.42 and AUM reached about INR23,000 crores (up 16.3%). Management said it sees motor pricing correcting in April and expects a regulatory response on expense of management (EOM) within 2-3 months.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Private car 44%, two-wheeler 32%, commercial vehicles 24% of business. OD/TP mix 38/62 vs industry 41/59. Own-damage loss ratio rose YoY; corrective action started, with impact expected from July-September quarter.

segments.name: Health (incl. group)
segments.commentary: Q4 health reinsurance non-renewal cost about INR252 crores (about INR200 crores in Q3). Retail is under 7% of health; employer-employee about 73% and non-employer-employee about 22%. Health market share about 1.3-1.4%.

segments.name: Fire / commercial
segments.commentary: Fire gross loss ratio 51% in FY26 vs 48% in FY25; net loss ratio rose on two large claims (INR55 crores gross in Q4). Cat treaty retention raised from INR36 crores to INR45 crores; earthquake limit raised from INR1,600 crores to INR2,000 crores.

segments.name: Two-wheeler
segments.commentary: Q4 two-wheeler premium was INR556 crores vs INR365 crores a year earlier, which pushed up EOM by about 3.5% in the quarter. Management estimates about 40% of FY26 two-wheeler business was new business.

segments.name: Crop
segments.commentary: Management plans to bid directly in government crop tenders this year, having previously written crop mainly through reinsurance acceptance; scheme structure not yet announced.

guidance_outlook: Management gives no numerical guidance; it said ROE and profitability are the focus.
Motor OD loss ratio expected to stabilise in July-September 2026 quarter and then fall; motor overall loss ratio targeted not to rise YoY in FY27.
New specialty commercial lines expected to reach about INR1,000 crores premium over 3-5 years.
Equity allocation at 8.5% of AUM with a 12.5% ceiling considered comfortable; fixed income duration at 4.5 years, with room to extend if rates rise.
Management expects EOM-related regulation within 2-3 months and expects the commission/management-expense split to be fixed.
Next year's effective tax rate expected at 25.2%.
capex_capacity: Reinsurance renewed for FY27: fire and other treaty capacity increased; property and engineering capacity raised with better commission terms.
A new miscellaneous treaty covers new risk types; an 11% quota share on non-motor, non-health premium was added to cap accumulation in Gujarat, Maharashtra and NCR.
Net retention for scooters and school buses was lowered through funds-withheld reinsurance after the Kolkata incident; management said this does not affect AUM.
Leverage rose to 5% (4.65% in June 2024); management expects it to hold around 5% over the next two years.
demand_pricing: Motor: management sees April 2026 price and commission correction in the market, and believes the market cannot sustain current prices. Growth outlook depends on the new-vehicle cycle, which was strong in H2 FY25.
Fire: softer terms seen in fire, but not in engineering, where growth was higher than fire. Fire market share about 3.9% on GWP.
Health: management plans to grow group health only if pricing improves by about 5%, and expects growth of 50-60% if loss ratio also falls by about 2%.
TP pricing: no motor TP hike this year; management said it is not privy to regulator thinking.
Competition: new non-life entrants are coming; management said it is not losing sleep over them and that EOM relief for new insurers should be split between commission and management expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Will fire profitability fall given higher cat reinsurance cost, net loss ratio deterioration, and a possibly softer fire market? Also, what is the crop strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is comfortable with fire profitability, citing better commission in fire and engineering and profit commission on earned premium. Crop: will bid directly in tenders this year, pending government scheme structure.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fairfax keep its stake after the reverse merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not spoken to Fairfax and said there is no news on the amalgamation timeline. Fairfax holds about 58%; going below 51% would trigger an open offer, and management does not expect a sale.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size of the new specialty commercial lines and what is the motor pricing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialty lines could reach about INR1,000 crores of premium in 3-5 years. Motor market correction in April 2026 on price and commission; overall motor loss ratio to be held flat or lower YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why did motor OD loss ratio rise and what is the retention and renewal data?
qa_highlights.answer: Management delayed corrective OD pricing to test retention and sold more SAOD in FY25. Motor retention fell to 89.6% from 95.9%. Renewal rates rose in private car across channels.

qa_highlights.question: How will EOM compliance be managed at company level and how does Indian acquisition cost compare internationally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said line-of-business mix explains the EOM gap and expects regulation to ease expense limits within 2-3 months. Management said Indian acquisition costs have risen over 20 years and cited RBI and Economic Survey commentary.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the discounting benefit and will long-run Ind AS investment yield match IGAAP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the discount-rate effect is stable unless rates move sharply; it moved to 7.09% from 6.9%. Management said investment decisions should be judged on ROE, not on mark-to-market, and that risk-based capital may favour companies with high equity allocation.

risks_watch: Own-damage motor loss ratio: corrective action is due to show from July-September 2026; the next two quarters are the test.
Motor retention fell to 89.6% from 95.9%; watch renewal rates and whether the market price correction affects volume.
Fire net loss ratio: two large claims lifted net loss ratio; the cat reinsurance cost rise may compress margins.
EOM regulation: timing and form of relief are unclear, and new entrants may bring forbearance on EOM.
Health: non-renewal of a reinsurance treaty cut Q4 GWP growth to 6.2%; health loss ratios remain a question.

Ind AS vs IGAAP comparability: the DAC unwind (about 65% of INR2,470 crores in FY26-27), the 25.2% tax rate, and the non-booking of INR303 crores of unearned premium (INR109 crores acquisition cost provided) will affect reported profit.
Fixed income duration and rates: duration is 4.5 years; an interest rate move could affect unrealised losses (INR99 crores at 31 March 2026).
summary.management_tone: Confident and defensive on reported numbers, pushing the Ind AS/DAC-based KPIs and ROE. Management was evasive on Fairfax, motor pricing timing, and specialty-line sizing, and offered no hard guidance.
key_quotes: And I think for all of you, analysts and fund managers, making comparisons would also become a lot more easier.
So on a loss ratio plus commission basis, which is how we always look at any product or any line of business, we should be seeing some improvement anyway.
Am I losing sleep because of new competition? Not really.
And if you feel that our loss ratio would be worse than anyone else in the market, we'll be more than happy to learn and put more pressure on our management team, including Jasleen to improve.
